newsitem.title: SPAIN: Uralita sees good future with disinvestment.
newsitem.headline: Uralita sees good future with disinvestment.

text.p: The outlook for the Spanish building material's group Uralita is positive thanks to planned disinvestment and the gradual recovery of the new home construction sector, Chairman Juan Antonio Garcia Diez.
"This year we are optimistic on the outlook," Garcia Diez told a news conference.
He said that the reduction in interest rates would have a stimulating effect on the housing market, the only part of the weak construction sector which is expected to clearly recover.

The group confirmed it expects attributable earnings of some four billion pesetas compared with 2.2 billion in 1996 and also expects to disinvest some six billion pesetas in a building and in two non-strategic units.
Uralita has designed a disinvestment plan of some 24 billion pesetas by the year 2000, of which some 15 billion will come from the sale of industrial stakes and another 10 billion in real estate.
In addition, some of these revenues will be returned to shareholders via reductions in nominal share value.
Specifically, this year the company plans to reduce its nominal share value by 40 pesetas to 400 pesetas this year if disinvestments follow plans.
Garcia Diez said shareholders remuneration will be a minimum payout of 35 percent, amortisation of its Treasury portfolio and a reduction in the nominal.
The company will pay a total dividend on 1996 results of 24 gross pesetas, plus 2.5 pesetas, compared with 44 pesetas in 1995. The company amortised three percent of its capital this year.
The group plans disinvestment in the chemical group Aragonesas of which it owns 49.5 percent, given it is not a strategic holding.
"Long-term we need to reduce our position in Aragonesas, but medium-term we believe it is a good investment," Garcia Diez said.
Uralita plans to invest some 65 billion pesetas by the year 2000, which will be drawn from earnings and disinvestment, in new acquisitions and in the construction of factories, he said.
But he said there would be no decision on the Latin American market before 1999.
